question: Should opaque `channelData` be recursively scanned and entirely suppressed whenever any nested key or value matches protected internal runtime context?
rationale: The code can implement either policy correctly, but only maintainers can decide the intended balance between preventing opaque-channel exfiltration and avoiding false-positive loss of provider-specific payload metadata.

options.title: Approve recursive fail-closed filtering
options.body: Accept whole-payload suppression on any protected-context match, then rebase and require green exact-head checks before merge.

options.title: Narrow the filtering contract
options.body: Define which opaque fields are user-visible or security-sensitive and adjust the sanitizer and tests before merge, accepting the maintenance cost of a narrower contract.

options.title: Pause stringified channelData support
options.body: Do not expand this outbound surface until a provider-neutral sanitization contract is established.

recommendation.title: Approve recursive fail-closed filtering
recommendation.body: Accept whole-payload suppression on any protected-context match, then rebase and require green exact-head checks before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest ownership of the message-action runner and message-tool boundary affected by this policy.
